title: Building Boxes
summary: Given an integer n, determine the least number of unit cubes that must touch the floor when n unit cubes are placed in a cubic room of side length n, with the condition that if a cube is placed on top of another, the sides of the lower cube must be adjacent to another cube or a wall.
statement: Given an integer n, determine the least number of unit cubes that must touch the floor when n unit cubes are placed in a cubic room of side length n, with the condition that if a cube is placed on top of another, the sides of the lower cube must be adjacent to another cube or a wall.
constraints: Stack n unit boxes in a cubic corner; every box not on the floor must have all four lower corners supported by boxes beneath it.
Return the minimum number of boxes touching the floor.
reference_solution:
def minimum_floor_boxes(n):
 used=floor=layer=0
 while used+layer*(layer+1)//2<=n:
  used+=layer*(layer+1)//2;floor+=layer;layer+=1
 extra=0
 while used<n:extra+=1;used+=extra
 return floor+extra

hints: Complete corner layers contribute triangular numbers of boxes and use one new floor row.
Build the largest complete tetrahedral stack, then extend the next floor row until the remainder is supported.
Accumulate layer*(layer+1)/2 while it fits; afterward add floor boxes whose cumulative support is 1+2+....
Complete layers are maximally support-efficient, and each extra floor box in the boundary row increases capacity by the next integer.

tests.explanation: All three boxes must touch the floor, so the answer is three.
A complete three-layer corner pyramid uses ten boxes and six floor positions.
